samples.summary: quoteDepth ignores the quote prefix's leading indentation, so blockquotes in different containers can be treated as the same one
samples.evidence: `quoteDepth` counts only `>` characters (`p.quote.length - p.quote.replace(/>/g,'').length`), but QUOTE_RE also captures up to three leading spaces (`/^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/`). So `  > - x` (a blockquote nested inside a list item's content) and `> - y` (a fresh top-level blockquote) both report depth 1, and `itemAbove`/`parentOf` (lines 159, 173) will pair them as siblings/parent even though they are different block containers. E.g. for `- a\n  > - x\n> - y`, indenting line 3 now yields `>   - y`, nesting it under an item that is not in its blockquote. The old prefix-text comparison rejected this pair. Column position, not just `>` count, determines the container.

samples.summary: The new depth guard's "leave the line alone" path still rewrites the line via prefixOf, normalising `[X]` to `[x]` (and tab-after-`]` to a space)
samples.evidence: `if (!p.marker || quoteDepth(p) !== depth) return prefixOf(p);` reconstructs the prefix instead of returning `p.line.text.slice(...)`. `parseLine` lowercases the checkbox (`check: m[4].toLowerCase()`, line 71) and `prefixOf` emits `[${check}] ` with exactly one space (line 94), so an untouched, different-depth line such as `>   - [X]\tc` is still changed to `>   - [x] c` and is pushed as an edit in `replacePrefixes` (line 244). The guard therefore does not fully honour the documented promise that lines in another container are left where they are; it silently edits their marker text.

samples.summary: Unreachable early return in shift skips the view.focus() that every other path performs
samples.evidence: `const top = lines.find((p) => p.marker); if (!top) return;` — both callers (`indentList` line 338, `outdentList` line 344) only call `shift` when a non-zero step was computed, which itself requires a marker line, so this branch is dead. If it ever were reached it would return without the `view.focus()` that `replacePrefixes` (line 262) always performs, leaving the editor unfocused after a toolbar click.

samples.summary: canIndent/canOutdent are computed from the top list line only, so the toolbar reports a move that shift now applies to just part of the selection
samples.evidence: `computeListState` derives `canIndent`/`canOutdent` from `indentStep`/`outdentStep`, which use `lines.find((p) => p.marker)` (lines 191, 210). `shift` now moves only lines whose `quoteDepth` equals the top line's (line 330). For a selection spanning a plain list and a quoted list (e.g. `- a\n- b\n>   - c`, lines 2–3) the button is enabled and the action silently changes only some of the selected lines, leaving the selection's structure partly shifted with no indication.

finding.summary: Removing the `quoted` skip leaves deeply-indented / tab-indented blockquote lines unprotected, so a toggle writes a marker in front of the `>` again
finding.evidence: The old guard used `QUOTED_RE = /^\s*>/` and `replacePrefixes` skipped any matching line. The new `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` only recognises a quote after at most three *spaces*, and the `if (p.quoted) continue;` skip in `replacePrefixes` was deleted (list-commands.ts:229-237). A line such as `\t> quote` or `    > quote` (a blockquote nested inside a list item, which the editor can produce) now parses with `quote === ''`, `marker === ''`, `content === '> quote'`, and `toggleBulletList` rewrites its prefix to `indent + '- '`, producing exactly the `- > quote` corruption the previous commit's comment says it was avoiding. Nothing else guards this path: `shift`, `toggleKind` and `replacePrefixes` all now write unconditionally.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree: QUOTE_RE at list-commands.ts:45 is /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/, which only accepts up to three literal spaces before `>`, so a tab-indented or 4+-space-indented blockquote line parses with quote='', indent=the whitespace, marker='', content='> quote' (parseLine, lines 49-63). replacePrefixes (234-263) contains no quoted/skip check at all, and toggleKind (273-300) therefore returns prefixOf({...p, marker:'-', gap:' '}) = indent + '- ' for such a line, writing the list marker in front of the `>` (e.g. `    > quote` -> `    - > quote`, `\t> quote` -> `\t- > quote`). That contradicts the file's own documented invariant (lines 21-27, 283-286) and the pinned behavior for shallow quotes (list-commands.test.ts:42-45 expects `> quoted item` -> `> - quoted item`), so the same toolbar action changes block structure instead of placing the marker inside the quote. The path is reachable in normal use: a blockquote nested inside a second-level list item sits at 4 spaces (item content column 4), and indentWithTab is bound in editor.ts:369,372 with tab-containing markdown also possible. No caller-side guard exists: selectedLines/targetLines/selectedTargets (108-135) filter only blank lines, and shift (323-334) and setTaskChecked (354-372) do not gate on quoting. In-lane (boundary/condition error producing wrong output and a broken invariant), so no refutation ground applies.
